records.title: Accelerating Transformer-based Deep Learning Models on FPGAs using Column Balanced Block Pruning
records.reason: IEEE publisher DOI could not be retrieved for primary full-text verification. Packet abstract indicates a concrete FPGA Transformer-inference pruning/acceleration result, so do not exclude it; retain as unresolved until hardware comparisons can be checked.

records.title: Rethinking Evaluation in ASR: Are Our Models Robust Enough?
records.reason: This is an evaluation of cross-dataset robustness for automatic speech recognition, not an LLM inference optimization.

records.title: Hardware Acceleration of Sparse and Irregular Tensor Computations of ML Models: A Survey and Insights
records.reason: Primary survey covers accelerator execution for sparse, irregular and quantized tensors across general ML/DNN workloads, including NLP. The hardware/kernel link to sparse-attention inference is credible, but it is a broad 2021 survey rather than a concrete LLM-specific method.

records.title: Proteina: Scaling Flow-based Protein Structure Generative Models
records.reason: Primary text shows protein-backbone generation with flow-based models and protein-specific scaling/training/sampling recipes. The cited compile lineage does not create an LLM inference efficiency contribution.

records.title: Scaling the Horizon, Not the Parameters: Reaching Trillion-Parameter Performance with a 35B Agent
records.reason: Primary method scales agent horizon and post-trains a 35B-A3B agent to approach larger-model performance, but the full text reports benchmark capability gains rather than inference tokens, latency, serving cost, or resource savings. Lower parameter count alone is insufficient evidence of an efficiency improvement.
